en: Lightning can strike the same location many times; for example, the Empire State Building gets struck by lightning about 25 times every year.
Weather describes day-to-day atmospheric conditions, while climate describes the average weather patterns in a place over at least 30 years.
Loam soil, a balanced mix of sand, silt, and clay, is the best soil for growing most crops because it holds water and nutrients well.
Pumice is a volcanic rock filled with tiny air bubbles that make it light enough to float on water.
Talc is the softest mineral on the Mohs hardness scale and can be easily scratched by a fingernail.
Water never truly disappears during evaporation; it changes from liquid to an invisible gas called water vapor and rises into the atmosphere.
The Sun is not burning like fire; it generates energy through nuclear fusion, which fuses hydrogen atoms into helium in its core.
Venus, not Mercury, is the hottest planet in our solar system because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat through a strong greenhouse effect.
Sirius, also called the Dog Star, is the brightest star visible in the night sky, not Polaris.
The Moon does not make its own light; it shines because its surface reflects sunlight toward Earth.
The Philippines has over 20 active volcanoes because it sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, a horseshoe-shaped zone of intense volcanic and earthquake activity.
Earthquakes occur when tectonic plates suddenly slide past each other along faults, releasing energy that shakes the ground.
